# terrakube_registry_provider (Resource)

A provider in the private registry of an organization. Set `imported` and `registry_namespace` to mirror a provider from the public registry, and Terrakube keeps its versions up to date. Destroying the provider also deletes its versions and their implementations, since Terrakube does not delete them for you.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "terrakube_organization" "org" {
  name = "my-organization"
}

# Mirror a provider from the public registry (Terrakube 2.30.0+). Terrakube keeps
# its versions up to date.
resource "terrakube_registry_provider" "aws" {
  organization_id    = data.terrakube_organization.org.id
  name               = "aws"
  description        = "AWS provider mirrored from the public registry"
  imported           = true
  registry_namespace = "hashicorp"
}

# A provider you build and host yourself.
resource "terrakube_registry_provider" "internal" {
  organization_id = data.terrakube_organization.org.id
  name            = "internal"
  description     = "Provider for our internal platform"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Provider name, for example `aws`. For an imported provider it is the name in the public registry.
- `organization_id` (String) Terrakube organization ID. Changing this forces a new resource.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Provider description
- `imported` (Boolean) Mirror the provider from the public registry. Needs `registry_namespace`. Terrakube 2.30.0+.
- `registry_namespace` (String) Namespace of the provider in the public registry, for example `hashicorp`. Only used when `imported` is true. Terrakube 2.30.0+.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Provider ID

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Registry provider can be imported with organization_id,id
terraform import terrakube_registry_provider.example 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000,00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
```
